planting.note: Can also be divided in fall; avoid disturbing roots more than necessary since the plant resents transplanting and recovers slowly.

directions: Pteridophyllum racemosum is a monotypic Japanese woodland perennial whose deeply cut, fern-like rosette of leaves gives the genus its name, even though it belongs to the poppy family rather than true ferns. In spring to early summer, slender racemes of small, four-petaled white flowers rise just above the foliage, echoing its native habitat on cool, shaded mountain slopes of Honshu. Plant divisions in consistently moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in full to partial shade sheltered from wind and summer heat, and disturb the roots as little as possible once established since it is slow to recover from transplanting. It performs best where summers stay cool, such as the Pacific Northwest or New England, where mature clumps become long-lived, low-maintenance woodland floor specimens for the collector's shade garden.
